0.original: Something seems to be weighing on Hermes's mind.

25.original: Speak with Meteion and have her accompany you.

26.original: Search for Doros while accompanied by Meteion.

49.original: I thoroughly enjoyed myself─at the end most of all!

50.original: All the creations are happy. That makes me happy too!

51.original: Tell me, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. In the course of watching me, have you learned aught of value?

53.original: Nothing so far, but I'm hopeful that will change.

55.original: I'm not sure what I'm looking for, but I don't think I've found it yet...

56.original: I see... If you told me what it is you seek, I would be able to better accommodate you.

57.original: Dynamis, you say? Curious that such an obscure phenomenon should be of interest to you.

58.original: If only my work were more interesting... Nevertheless, I'm still indebted to you for keeping Meteion company. If there is aught I might do, you need but ask.

59.original: Chief Hermes, what good fortune to find you here.

61.original: The lykaon─I'm afraid it's done it again.

62.original: No sooner did we release one for observation than it set upon the nearby okyupetes, slaughtering them.

63.original: Was the creature hungry? Or somehow provoked?

64.original: I had just fed them myself, and the okyupetes were keeping a wide berth. It is the nature of the lykaon that is to blame. Their innate viciousness.

65.original: Temperament aside, it is an outstanding creation, perfect in form and function.

66.original: Though it may not be suited for release, I've no doubt that the bureau will accept its concept for preservation.

67.original: In any case, there's no point in postponing the inevitable. Doros will revert them all once the paperwork is in order.

68.original: Where is the scene of the incident?

69.original: Just off the path to the Twelve Wonders. As you make your way, you should see it on the left. I don't know if Doros is still there, however.

71.original: If this is part of his work, then I would observe. We follow.

72.original: A fearsome beast, this lykaon... But where is it now?

73.original: The okyupete is no easy prey. With its hooves and horns, it was designed to be formidable even on land.

74.original: Yet they didn't stand a chance against the lykaon...

76.original: The lacerations and burns are unmistakable. A lykaon was indeed responsible.

77.original: But the creature is nowhere to be seen. Doros must have taken it away.

78.original: The man makes his base at the Twelve Wonders. I shall go and seek him out there.

79.original: Emet-Selch and I will search the area for good measure. Just to make sure the lykaon did not escape.

80.original: My thanks. Let us meet at the Twelve Wonders when you have finished.

81.original: I will go on ahead. Please follow with <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>.

82.original: Come, come. It's down this path and over the bridge.

83.original: There it is─the Twelve Wonders. Hermes is looking for Doros. Let's look for Doros too!

84.original: He's a man with long, blond hair...I think. I'll know him when I see him!

85.original: Meteion is now accompanying you. Keep her at your side in order to proceed with quest objectives.

86.original: You can leave Meteion behind by entering a different area, or by speaking with her and selecting the option to part ways.

87.original: If you wish to have Meteion accompany you again, return and speak with her at the original location.

92.original: Come on, let's find Doros. He's a man with long, blond hair...I think!

93.original: Are you sure you wish to part ways with Meteion?

94.original: All right! I'll wait in front of the Twelve Wonders.

95.original: Ready to look for Doros again? Let's go, let's go!

96.original: Meteion has yet to arrive. Be sure she is at your side before attempting to continue.

98.original: You recall that you do not actually know what Doros looks like. You should have Meteion accompanying you before initiating conversation.

99.original: ...Hm? If you're with Meteion, then I assume you're on an errand for Hermes. What can I do for you?

100.original: S-Sorry, wrong person! We're looking for Doros...

101.original: Ah, I see. We do have similar hair, so people often mistake us from afar. I hope you find him soon.

102.original: Don't worry, you're hardly the first ones to mistake me for Doros, and you certainly won't be the last.

103.original: Once I get back and record today's results, I should finally be able to put that report to bed...

104.original: Once I get back and record today's results, I should finally be able to put that report to bed...

105.original: Not Doros! His hair is long, but the color is wrong.

106.original: ...Doros? I think he returned a short while ago.

107.original: You recall that you do not actually know what Doros looks like. You should have Meteion accompanying you before initiating conversation.

109.original: Well now, if it isn't Meteion. What brings you here?

110.original: Ah, I thought I heard familiar voices!

111.original: I didn't realize you two had decided to help me search for Doros. Thank you.

112.original: You're in charge of the lykaones, I believe. Where are they now?

113.original: (-Doros-)Out in the fields in restraints. Frenzied as they were, I couldn't well return them to Ktisis.

114.original: (-Doros-)Once I've submitted my report, I'll see them reverted without delay.

115.original: It's as he says. The beasts are indeed quite ferocious.

116.original: (-Doros-)Y-You're one of the Fourteen! Wh-What brings you here!?

117.original: Nothing you need concern yourself with. As you were.

118.original: We've heard the news─that a lykaon slaughtered okyupetes. As the observer in charge, you are of the opinion that they are not fit to be released?

119.original: (-Doros-)Aye, I am. Their abnormal aggression and exceptional strength makes for a highly problematic combination.

120.original: (-Doros-)It matters not where they are released. Lykaones would threaten other species and upset the natural order.

121.original: Could it be that the specimens observed are an outlier?

122.original: (-Doros-)Highly unlikely. We've created a good many of them; all exhibited the same tendencies.

123.original: (-Doros-)Even when we used Kairos to begin with a fresh slate, their behavior was unchanged.

125.original: (-Doros-)A memory reconfiguration system. The chief himself created it.

126.original: (-Doros-)It allows us to erase or alter memories, that we may observe creations in different environmental conditions without needing to remake them from scratch.

127.original: Quite impressive...and potentially dangerous. Depending on the intensity of the aetheric emissions, Pashtarot may wish to have words with you.

128.original: Rest assured I've kept all values within prescribed limits. And to prevent misuse, its applications are limited to those authorized by the chief overseer.

129.original: Do not misunderstand. To manipulate a subject's memories is an intrusive act I deeply abhor. But it is still preferable to execution.

130.original: (-Doros-)Come now, Chief, let's not be so melodramatic! What was born of aether is simply being reduced to its original state.

131.original: (-Doros-)I know the distinctions concern you, but we mustn't lose sight of the bigger picture─making rational choices for the sake of a more prosperous star.

132.original: (-Doros-)If a creation cannot be properly studied even with the aid of Kairos, we remake it. If a creation is deemed a detrimental existence, we unmake it. 'Tis all for the greater good, and none question the necessity of such routine processes.

133.original: I understand these things, I do. I would never think to unleash a clear and undeniable threat unto the world.

134.original: Yet insignificant though their individual lives may be next to all creation, it is all the lykaones have.

135.original: Before we seal their fates, we owe it to these beings to exhaust all options. To ensure that nothing has been overlooked.

136.original: (-Doros-)If you insist. Let me provide you with a full report, and we may take it from there.

137.original: Would it be possible for us to attend the discussion? That Emet-Selch may better carry out his duties.

139.original: Pray show them to the meeting room.

140.original: We have a duty to the star, this I know. But it doesn't mean we don't also have a responsibility to the lives we bring into existence here.

141.original: To man, other beings are just things. To be used and controlled. Like magic.

142.original: That's what Hermes told me once...
